Key UI Variables & Their Legal Basis:

Company Country Factor (The Master Switch):

UI Impact: The calculation remains idle unless the "Company" is linked to "Saudi Arabia".

System Logic: Automated Saudi Gratuity Calculation
Data Source: Employee Profile
The system automatically fetches the following fields from the Employee Record to trigger the calculation:

Company Country: If the employee's company is in "Saudi Arabia", the Saudi Labor Law engine is activated.

Employment Type: The calculation is applied specifically for "Permanent" contracts.

Reason of Leaving: This is the primary factor for Article 85 (Resignation rules).

Statutory Rules Applied:

General Award (Article 84):

0–5 Years: 15 days' wage per year.

5+ Years: 30 days' wage per year.

Resignation Rule (Article 85):

< 2 Years: 0% payout.

2 to < 5 Years: 33.33% (1/3) payout.

5 to < 10 Years: 66.66% (2/3) payout.

10+ Years: 100% (Full) payout
Employment Type Validation:

UI Impact: Filters for "Permanent" status.

Legal Basis: Gratuity is a statutory right for indefinite/fixed-term contracts; temporary or internship contracts follow different settlement protocols.

Base Wage Unit (The Salary):

UI Impact: Extracts "Monthly Total" (Basic + Fixed Allowances).

Legal Basis (Article 2): Defines "Wage" as the actual wage plus all other scheduled increments and allowances. The EOSG is calculated based on the last wage drawn by the worker.

Service Brackets (Article 84):

UI Impact: Calculated from "Joining Date" to "Relieving Date".

Legal Basis (Article 84): A worker is entitled to an award of half-month's wage for each of the first five years and a full month's wage for each subsequent year.

The Multiplier (Article 85 - Resignation):

UI Impact: Most critical field. If "Resignation" is selected, the following legal multipliers are applied to the total amount:

Service < 2 Years: No entitlement (0 payout).

Service 2 to 5 Years: One-third (1/3) of the award.

Service 5 to 10 Years: Two-thirds (2/3) of the award.

Service 10+ Years: Full award (100% payout).

Legal Basis (Article 85): Specifically governs cases where the work relationship ends due to the worker's resignation, defining the exact percentage of the award based on seniority.

Automatic Table Sync:

UI Impact: Any change in the above fields forces a recalculation.

Legal Basis (Article 88): Ensures the employer pays the worker's wages and settles their entitlements promptly (within one week of termination or two weeks of resignation).
1. General Rule (Article 84)
The worker is entitled to an end-of-service award as follows:

First 5 Years: Half a month's wage for each year.

Subsequent Years (Beyond the 5th): One full month's wage for each year.

Pro-rata: The award is calculated for parts of the year in proportion to the time spent in service.

2. In Case of Resignation (Article 85)
If the work relationship ends due to the worker's resignation, the entitlement is adjusted based on the duration of service:

Less than 2 years: No entitlement.

2 to less than 5 years: One-third (1/3) of the award.

5 to less than 10 years: Two-thirds (2/3) of the award.

10 years or more: Full award entitlement.
